findings.detail: The medium appends generic catalog and downstream-effects language unrelated to Spanberger’s selection. The long repeatedly explains that consequences were not supplied and closes by spelling out the record’s evidentiary limits; those caveats take up more space than the actual context of the opposition response and its political significance.
The medium appends generic standalone-event and downstream-effects prose to the ranch-sale report.

The long devotes most of its space to listing details the summary omits and disclaiming any Trump connection or wrongdoing, then says what “the record therefore preserves.” It gives no additional event-specific account beyond the sale, buyer family, date, and price already in the supplied context.
The medium appends generic standalone-event and institutional-effects language unrelated to Gail Slater’s departure from the Justice Department.
The medium appends generic catalog and downstream-effects text rather than describing the poll result.

The long repeats the same caution about causation and missing poll details several times: the shootings are not shown to cause the change, survey particulars are absent, and the comparison is not a causal estimate. The poll figures and dated comparison provide the substantive context; the repeated caveats crowd it out.
The medium includes generic standalone-event and downstream-effects prose unrelated to Infantino’s planned Uefa appearance.

The long repeatedly narrates what the supplied headline/summary does and does not establish, including that it gives no basis for concluding Trump threatened Infantino or changed Uefa policy. This packet-audit framing overwhelms the limited reader-facing account of the reported scrutiny.

The medium appends generic standalone-event and downstream-effects claims to the report about Cubans facing deportation. The long adds reported examples and policy context in readable prose; the defect lies in the medium.
The medium appends the generic standalone-event and downstream-effects template to the report about Sean Plankey’s removal from his DHS adviser post.

The long calls the episode “cataloged as a distinct Trump-related incident,” then speculates about political pressure, institutional stress, and public-trust effects not established in the supplied context. This internal classification and consequence padding is not a reader-facing account of the removal.

The medium appends generic standalone-event and downstream-effects language to the Senate vote report. The long adds the vote, resolution, procedural consequence, and unresolved war-powers question in concrete terms.

The supplied context says a New York Times report described a CIA weapons program for Iranian Kurdish forces that began before the current war. The long instead attributes public remarks about an incursion to “former President Donald Trump” and claims he framed it as strategy, neither of which appears in the supplied context; the title/synopsis do not support this account of the event.
The long mentions “notes attached to the entry,” names an assigned category, and calls for additional reporting. This is internal packet/category commentary rather than an account for readers.

The medium appends generic standalone-event and downstream-effects claims to a brief about Trump’s changing rationale for Iran strikes and primary results. The long adds the specific public rationales and distinguishes the separate primary-results segment.
